questions.prompt: Out of position, the default start for a preflop caller is…

choices.text: Check, then decide to call, raise, or fold against a bet.

questions.explanation: Leading into the raiser is the exception. Checking keeps the raiser’s bluffs in the pot.

choices.text: Strong made hands and some strong draws, not every missed hand.
Only the nuts, never a draw

questions.explanation: You build the pot when you are ahead or have a lot of equity, and you fold out better one-pair hands with some draws.

choices.text: Medium made hands and decent draws that cannot raise for value.
The nuts, which should usually raise
A hand you will stack off with no pair and no draw

questions.explanation: Call when you beat bluffs or have equity. Do not call when you beat nothing and cannot improve.

questions.prompt: A donk bet can make sense when…

choices.text: The flop hits your calling range much harder than the raiser’s range.
You have bottom pair on ace-high
You want to bet air because you act first

questions.explanation: Leading 876 after you called in the big blind is more reasonable than leading A72 into the raiser.
